# Width, trace, and normalized error ledger

Source audit for PR #1194 head `735a85c0c2e64a723bcdc08ba59a4259ad6ed176`.
Original source pin: `CocoSgt/riemann-hypothesis-lean@7cbf7a0c32fca1badf05931879a37c3f8a2b03b4`.
All `src/` paths below are relative to `/workspace/scratch/847cedbb0d50/geometric-closure/audit/upstream-source`.
This is a static source and algebra review; no local Lean or Lake was executed.

## Finding

The original geometric construction has a real, very large squared-norm allowance, `exp(2*b)`, with the SAME `b = exp(x^eps)` used by its weight windows. Its actual proof bounds the paid logarithm by `z^10 <= b`, so at least `b` remains inside the `2*b` allowance. An additional factor `4^j` on this same joint squared norm would fit whenever `j*log 4 <= b`, without enlarging the final slope allowance.

This is a conditional numerical entry point, not an attachment theorem for a signed commutator. The existing maps, source and target lattices, norms, injectivity, integral preservation, and target/source rank comparison all have to remain the ones in `MapsAt`. No source or native theorem inspected identifies the diagnostic jet order with this construction's rank parameters, or identifies the proposed R-fold commutator with these maps.

The width disappears when the FINAL arithmetic error is divided by its main coefficient. Consequently an exponential factor inserted only at that final stage is not paid by choosing a large width. Nor does the whole trace error have exponential slack: its chosen sampling contribution is polynomial, even though two of its primitive trace tolerances are stretched exponential.

## 1. Actual parameters; distinguish the repeated names

| Quantity | Exact source definition / condition | Declaration path |
|---|---|---|
| `x`, `eps` | `1 < x`, `0 < eps < 1/52` | `Formalism/LocalRingCardinality/DataParams₂.lean`, `Scale` |
| `ez` | `eps/J`, with `1 <= J`; not automatically the same exponent as every later analytic epsilon | Same file, `Scale.ez` |
| `L` | `x^eps` | Same file, `Scale.L` |
| `b` | `exp L = exp(x^eps)` | Same file, `Scale.b` |
| `a` | `x*b` | Same file, `Scale.a` |
| `X'`, `b'` | `exp(x^(eps/3))`, `a/X'` | Same file, `Scale.X'`, `Scale.b'` |
| `w''` | `b'/(x*n) = b/(n*X')` for positive `x,n` | Same file, `Scale.w''` |
| `X''` | `a/w'' = x*n*X'` for positive `x,n` | Same file, `Scale.X''` |
| `n`, `f`, `r` | `n=ord`, `f=2*n`, `r=k_source+m-1` | `Formalism/LocalRingCardinality/Params.lean`, `Ranks` |
| `z` | `f*r*L`; all factors come from the SAME datum | `Formalism/LocalRingCardinality/DataParamsT.lean`, `zBase` |
| `PP` | `CP*z^eP`, `1<=CP`, `12<=eP`; also explicit polynomial and room inequalities | Same file, `ParamsT` |
| `kappa` | Sum of absolute values of actual `laOf` weights over CM embeddings and weight coordinates | `Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Definitions/Divisors/NormNegCmConstantEqAtAllEmbeddings.lean`, `sizeK`; `CovolXOfCovol.lean`, `kap` |
| `delta` in descent | `b/(PP*kappa)` | `Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/DivisorProofs/LowerBoundOfAllEstimates.lean`, `lowAt_of_cover` |
| `n_T` | Cardinality of the actual top set `TT`, proved by the equivalence `eT`; not a free averaging count | `Development/AutomorphicArithmetic/DedekindLFunctions/LandauTheorems/ChTop.lean`, `ch_top` |

`Scale.delta1 = x^(-eps/8)` is an orbit/window density and is distinct from the descent rank defect `delta=b/(PP*kappa)` and the trace rank defect `delBar=E7`.

The analytic text-scale definitions `bTx`, `aTx`, `XpTx`, `bpTx`, `wppTx`, `XppTx` in `Formalism/SizeWindowBrackets/ErrorFormsWeakWindowsFalse.lean` have exactly the same formulas when their `x,epsilon` are identified. A full application still needs its explicit same-parameter and same-object identifications; equal-looking variable names do not supply those.

## 2. Where the geometric cost is really paid

`Development/AbelianVarietyTheory/Proofs/DivisorProofs/MapsBoundOfDeepGood.lean`, theorem `GlobalTheory.CovTop.DescentMaps.maps`, sets `z=zBase(L)` and derives

\[
 z\ge 2C+200,\qquad z^{12}\le b,\qquad
 \log q_{\rm map}\le45z^2.
\]

For the actual group `grpHR fr`, the exact collective bill is

\[
 q_{\rm map}^{3}\exp(Cz^9)^2
 =\exp(3\log q_{\rm map}+2Cz^9).
\]

The proof itself yields

\[
 3\log q_{\rm map}+2Cz^9
 \le135z^2+2Cz^9
 \le(135+2C)z^9
 \le z^{10}\le z^{12}\le b.
\]

The stated consumer only requires the weaker upper bound `exp(2*b)`. The native reconstruction is `RHLean/Geometry/NativeDescentCostPayment.lean`, `nativeDescent_collectiveNormBudget`, with hypotheses `q>0`, `C>=0`, `log q<=45*z^2`, `2*C+200<=z`, and `z^12<=b`.

Thus a factor `4^j` multiplying this SAME joint square-norm bill can be paid if

\[
 j\log4\le 2b-3\log q_{\rm map}-2Cz^9.
\]

The sufficient inequality `j*log 4 <= b` uses the existing proved slack. For example, the extra relation `j<=z` would suffice, because `log4<2`, `z>=200`, and `2z<=z^12<=b`. This relation is NOT currently proved for the diagnostic jet. For a physical choice `j=R` and `x` comparable to `R^2`, the numerical inequality is eventually compatible with `b=exp(x^eps)` for fixed positive `eps`; that asymptotic compatibility is also not the missing map/norm attachment.

The actual consumer is `MapsAt` in `CovolXOfCovol.lean`:

\[
 \sum_h \|\phi_h(f)\|_{\sigma}^{2}\le e^{2b}\|f\|_{\sigma}^{2},
\]

with integral preservation, joint injectivity, and a bound on the full joint target rank. `RkAt` bounds that rank ratio by `1+b/(PP*kappa)`; `GminAt` supplies actual target generators with norm at most `exp(PP*kappa)`. The ensuing determinant argument uses

\[
 P=b,\quad\Lambda=PP\kappa,\quad\delta=b/(PP\kappa),
 \qquad\delta\,(2\Lambda)=2b.
\]

This is explicit rank-height payment. It is not a freely chosen rescaling. `SizeAt` additionally requires `1<=b<=unitE`, `|mainT|<=PP*kappa`, and `b<=PP*kappa`, among its other original conditions. `LowerBoundOfAllEstimates.lowAt_of_cover` then obtains

\[
 -\operatorname{mainT}-(2(C_F+C_U)+9)\operatorname{unitE}\le\mu_{\rm core}.
\]

An inverse coercivity constant and an upper operator bound have different orientations. A proof that a commutator's inverse coercivity cost enters the displayed `MapsAt` upper square-norm bill is required before applying this available room to it.

## 3. Trace tolerance and the strong error window

`Formalism/SizeWindowBrackets/SlopesFromSizeAndCount.lean` defines

\[
 E_8=e^{-x^{\epsilon/8}},\quad E_7=e^{-x^{\epsilon/7}},\quad
 \overline\delta=E_7,\quad\overline\eta=6x^{-c_{HH}},\quad
 \overline e=2E_8^2.
\]

Its `FamC.TraceIn` requires the actual Hilbert--Schmidt `InputS`, integral row factorization, matrix/isometry identities, and

\[
 -1\le\eta_0\le E_8,\quad\eta_1\le E_8,\quad
 0\le e_0,\quad\sqrt{e_0}\le E_8,
 \qquad(1-E_7)D_{\rm all}\le D.
\]

These are actual trace/matrix conditions, not consequences of merely setting `b`. The theorem `inputs_fourth_to_third` in `ChainSlopeWindows/AnalyticFirstToLatticeDiscriminant.lean` transfers them, plus `Inputs6d` and the original size conditions, to the strong window. In particular it proves `4*sqrt(2*E8^2)<=x^(-cHH)` and hence

\[
 (\overline\eta+4\sqrt{\overline e})x^{c_{HH}}b
 =\left(6+4\sqrt2\,x^{c_{HH}}e^{-x^{\epsilon/8}}\right)b
 \le7b.
\]

`ErrWindows` requires

\[
 (\overline\eta+4\sqrt{\overline e})x^{c_{HH}}b
 \le K x^\epsilon n_T a.
\]

The full error contains this multiplied by `(1-delBar)^(-1)`, at most 2 under the original bounds. The source proves that the weaker conditions `etaBar<=1`, `eBar<=1` do not suffice: `ChainSlopeWindows/SubThreeMulLogTwoLe.lean`, `error_sizes_weak_false`.

If `4^j` multiplies the WHOLE trace contribution, its necessary numerical comparison after `a=xb` is

\[
 4^j\left(6+4\sqrt2\,x^{c_{HH}}e^{-x^{\epsilon/8}}\right)
 \le K n_T x^{1+\epsilon}.
\]

There is only polynomial room here when `n_T` is polynomial in `x`. If an added cost instead affects only a primitive exponentially small error, its norm convention matters. In particular, multiplying the SQUARED error `eBar` by `4^j` changes

\[
 4\sqrt{\overline e}\quad\hbox{to}\quad
 4\sqrt{4^j\overline e}=4\,2^j\sqrt{\overline e}.
\]

For the actual choice `eBar=2*E8^2`, this contribution, before multiplying by `b`, becomes

\[
 4\sqrt2\exp\left(j\log2+c_{HH}\log x-x^{\epsilon/8}\right).
\]

Keeping the source's bound of this contribution by 1 would require
`j*log 2 + cHH*log x + log(4*sqrt 2) <= x^(epsilon/8)`.
By contrast, multiplying an already-linear `E8` contribution by `4^j` requires the analogous comparison with `j*log4`. Multiplying the WHOLE trace expression by `4^j` also multiplies the nondecaying term 6 and is governed by the preceding polynomial comparison. None of these three operations is interchangeable, and no unused exponential margin at these trace entry points has been proved for the diagnostic jet. One cannot apply the stretched-exponential tolerance to the polynomial sampling term `6*x^(-cHH)`.

## 4. Full normalized arithmetic error

Write `n=|H|`, `T=|TT|`, `U=|T2|`, and `Delta=U/n>0`. The source `BNBoundsU` in `DedekindLFunctions/SplitInertia.lean` retains

\[
 B_0\le2nmbx^\epsilon,\qquad
 N_c\le\frac{Ukbx^\epsilon}{n(nx^{-\epsilon})}.
\]

`ch_top` uses the SAME `IdentU` data and the eleven-part analytic `LChain.SizeData₂`, the strong `ErrWindows`, `BNBoundsU`, and `LargeX` to prove a uniform gap bound with

\[
 \operatorname{Err}=x^{C\epsilon}
 \left[T a_E\left(1+\frac{m^2}{k_s}\right)
 +m\left(2nmbx^\epsilon+\frac{Uk_sbx^\epsilon}{n(nx^{-\epsilon})}\right)\right],
 \qquad C=e_{Div}+e_{Loss}+3.
\]

`CharacterBalanceMoves.core` in `LandauTheorems/ChCore.lean` proves the exact main coefficient

\[
 Q=Tmb\frac{\Delta}{2},\qquad
 QY\le\operatorname{Err}+\frac{2Tmb}{x}.
\]

After division by positive `Q`, with every original density and factor retained,

\[
 Y\le x^{C\epsilon}\left[
 \frac{2a_E}{mb\Delta}\left(1+\frac{m^2}{k_s}\right)
 +\frac{4nm x^\epsilon}{T\Delta}
 +\frac{2k_sx^{2\epsilon}}{nT}\right]
 +\frac4{\Delta x}.
\]

For `a_E=xb`, the first coefficient becomes `2x/(m*Delta)`. Every `b` cancels. The weaker allowed bound `a_E<=2*x*b` increases that coefficient to at most `4x/(m*Delta)`; it does not leave decay in `b`.

The hypotheses retained by this step include actual `HostFactsS`, `SizesA`, `ThinScales`, `CostWindows`, containment `T2 subset A0`, a gap bound for every `u in A0`, and the actual retained-character lower bound. `IdentU` equates the same weight family, arithmetic ASK sums, Euler constant, and logarithmic derivative; it is not an abstract equivalence of numerical budgets. The eleven clauses in analytic `SizeData₂` are HidaSetting, DIV, EComp5, HComp, Count5, Slopes, QuotientSlopeBoundsWith, LossBounds, SlopeIneq, HHBound, and FParams.

The original remaining windows are

\[
 T\ge\tfrac12 n x^{-\epsilon/8},\quad\Delta\ge x^{-\epsilon},\quad
 x^{1/2-\epsilon}\le m\le x^{1/2+\epsilon/2},\quad
 xm\le k_s\le n^2x^{1/2-\epsilon},
\]

plus an explicit polynomial upper bound on `k_s`. `CostWindows` retains both
`2*f*(x+1)*theta <= 1/x` and `6*f*(x+1)*(eta+1) <= b/x`.
No relation in these formulas identifies `k_s` with the prime-free diagnostic jet order. The downstream character bound still contains the excluded-character sum `SigA`; it cannot be removed by width normalization.

## 5. Exact scope of the conclusion

There is a genuine candidate geometric payment scalar: the unused logarithmic room in the original collective squared-norm budget, together with the exact rank-defect/height payment. There is no free exponential saving at the final `Err/Q` stage, and the whole trace term cannot absorb `4^j` merely from its chosen `E8` component. Whether the commutator test is already paid therefore depends on the actual consumer and norm orientation, not the size of the isolated diagnostic constant.

The next proof obligation is a same-object attachment or a demonstration that the finite-dimensional coercivity constant is discarded before every quantitative consumer. No new assumption or Lean interface was added by this audit.
